tickets.text: Inspect before changing. Read applicable repository instructions, inventory files, detect package managers and runtimes, inspect Git status, and identify existing user changes.

Record architecture decisions. Write ADRs for database-backed workflow, SQLite/PostgreSQL parity, browser-owned external commits, free-only inference, canonical candidate facts, and the deployment profiles.

Establish the requirement ledger. Create records for R01-R12, every phase, and each acceptance gate with status, dependencies, evidence paths, last tested commit, and unresolved external prerequisites.

Define scope and support claims. Create an initial adapter matrix with mock-only, planned, fixture-tested, dry-run-tested, and live-verified levels, separating discovery support from submission support.
Plan reference reuse. Record upstream commit and license, candidate files, modifications needed, and tests required before import.

gates.requirement: Every R01-R12 requirement maps to at least one implementation phase and a verification method.
The architecture contains exactly one authoritative application state store per deployment.
The first genuine submission milestone is P08, not hidden behind a later optional agent framework.

A clean-room reader can identify how to start, where private configuration belongs, and how progress is recorded.

phases.title: Runnable skeleton, developer experience, and CI

tickets.text: Scaffold boundaries. Create the apps and packages listed in chapter 05, implementing only necessary initial modules with shared schemas, typed errors, structured logging, and configuration validation.
Define runtime profiles. Support explicit demo, local, and server configuration types, and default a public clone to demo with synthetic data and external submission disabled.
Build health surfaces. Add version, liveness, readiness, and worker-heartbeat endpoints; readiness must fail for unavailable required persistence rather than returning HTTP 200.

Create the dashboard shell. Show source jobs, application stages, exceptions, workers, and settings using synthetic data with accessible keyboard navigation and clear empty, loading, and error states.
Establish CI. Run formatting, linting, type checking, unit tests, dependency checks, and a production build with deterministic fixtures and a pinned lockfile.

gates.requirement: A clean clone installs and starts using the documented process.
The API, worker, and UI show consistent version and environment information.
Invalid or missing configuration causes an actionable startup error.

CI passes without external paid services or candidate accounts.

phases.title: Persistence, durable work, and audit events

tickets.text: Schema and migrations. Create owner, candidate version, source, job, application, task, attempt, artifact, authorization, exception, and audit/outbox records with foreign keys, uniqueness constraints, timestamps, schema versions, and migration tests.
Repository interfaces. Implement transaction boundaries and typed query methods, keeping backend-specific lease SQL inside persistence.
Queue worker. Implement claim, heartbeat, lease renewal, retry-wait, cancellation, dead letter, and success acknowledgment with application-level and domain-level concurrency limits.
Pure state machine. Reject invalid transitions and stale revisions, distinguishing retryable preparation from externally ambiguous attempts.
Outbox and audit. Atomically persist state plus event, then deliver events idempotently, redacting sensitive fields by schema.

gates.requirement: Concurrent claims produce one owner for each task and one committing owner per application.
Killing a worker during a preparation task results in recoverable requeue after lease expiry.
Killing a worker after an in-flight attempt creates reconciliation work, not a fresh submission task.
At-least-once outbox delivery produces no duplicate downstream side effect.
The same repository contract suite passes on SQLite and PostgreSQL.
A migration from the previous schema retains application identity and audit history.
Disk-full and database-unavailable errors prevent new external commits.

tickets.text: Source ingestion. Import DOCX/PDF files without modifying originals; extract text, tables, hyperlinks, and source locators, and store file hashes and parsing quality.

Fact ledger. Create typed employment, education, skills, language, project, metric, availability, and work-authorization facts with explicit extracted, owner-asserted, verified, conflicting, or expired status.
Chronology validation. Compute experience in non-overlapping months, track full-time and part-time distinctions, and flag inconsistent dates or technologies assigned to implausible periods.

Owner policy. Build onboarding for role scope, location, sponsorship wording, salary answers, account creation, optional disclosures, blocked employers, and daily submission limit, with review-only, fill-only, and auto-submit modes.
Answer memory. Store approved semantic answers with valid dates, scope, exact meaning, and evidence, with a reusable review mechanism that resolves the same question across pending applications.

gates.requirement: Every material candidate claim is traceable to a source or explicit owner assertion.
Overlapping employment does not inflate computed experience.
A profile revision invalidates affected prepared packets while preserving historical ones.
Revoking auto-submit blocks new commits immediately at the policy gate.
Missing salary or ambiguous sponsorship answers create targeted exceptions without blocking unrelated applications.
The public repository contains synthetic examples only.
The user can export and inspect the exact active authorization in plain language.

phases.title: Discovery, job identity, and historical imports

tickets.text: Connector SDK. Implement source configuration, pagination, incremental polling, rate policy, raw snapshots, normalized output, and health metrics, with fixture replay mode and robust timeout and error classes.

Canonical identity. Resolve requisition IDs, application URLs, employers, source aliases, and likely cross-postings, keeping suspected duplicates reversible.
Historical import. Import existing application records and document-folder metadata, preserving user-asserted submitted status separately from independent receipts.
Watchlist and freshness. Add Netherlands company lists, role aliases, first-seen, posted, and updated times, closure detection, and source-specific polling schedules.

gates.requirement: Repeated polling of the same feed creates no duplicate jobs or application work.
Pagination and delta cursors do not omit records across fixture boundary cases.
Closed, temporarily missing, and parser-failed states remain distinguishable.
Cross-postings map to one application where identity is established.
Historical user-asserted submissions block accidental repeat applications without inflating new confirmed totals.
Source 403/429 responses activate the configured pause/backoff behavior.
At least one real current vacancy can be read, normalized, and displayed with source evidence, without submitting it.

phases.title: Free-only inference and evaluated matching

tickets.text: Gateway policy. Implement model discovery, current price and capability checks, route allowlists, privacy settings, account-level budget reservation, timeout handling, and a no-paid-tools default.
Resilience. Add schema validation, bounded repair, expiring model health, rate-limit backoff, daily-budget exhaustion states, and redacted request logs.
Deterministic gates. Implement location, language, duplicate, closure, salary-feasibility, and explicit sponsorship restrictions from typed facts and requirements.
Semantic assessment. Extract requirements with evidence spans, map them to candidate fact IDs, and compute the final weighted score in code.

Evaluation dataset. Create at least 50 labeled, sanitized examples covering strong matches, adjacent roles, hard disqualifiers, ambiguous sponsorship, seniority mismatch, and misleading titles, with an untouched holdout subset.

gates.requirement: A manually pinned paid model is rejected in free-only mode.
An unknown price field or paid tool configuration is rejected before inference.
Quota reservations remain consistent under concurrent requests and restarts.
A 429 does not trigger account/key rotation or unbounded retry.
A schema-valid but unsupported candidate claim is rejected.
The ranking evaluation report includes held-out errors and score-component explanations.
Lack of an eligible free route pauses inference but leaves discovery and deterministic work operational.

phases.title: Tailored CVs, letters, and answer packets

tickets.text: Content schemas. Define CV, letter, claim, and answer ASTs with fact references, length constraints, and template versions, with no executable model-authored markup.

Generation. Implement professional-evidence-first bullet selection, role-specific summaries, concise motivation letters, and semantic answer reuse, keeping dates, employers, degrees, and metrics immutable.
Validation. Check claim support, years-of-experience wording, company and role correctness, language requirements, tense and delivery status, and absence of placeholders or another employer's name.
Rendering. Produce DOCX and PDF from the pinned pipeline with extraction checks, layout bounds, page limits, visual golden tests, and upload-size constraints.
Packet store. Write immutable manifests and content-addressed artifacts, exporting user-readable copies without overwriting originals.

gates.requirement: Every material generated claim links to approved evidence and passes independent validation.
A prototype cannot be described as deployed in the test set.
Hands-on and professional experience totals remain distinct.
All representative PDFs render without clipping, unreadable text, or missing sections.
DOCX and PDF contain equivalent candidate facts and company/role references.
A changed artifact hash invalidates an existing readiness/intent record.
A model outage still permits approved deterministic packets, while unresolved substantive questions are deferred.

phases.title: Mock ATS and browser filling contract

tickets.text: Mock ATS server. Build synthetic job pages and forms with server-side application records, unique application IDs, configurable failure points, uploads, conditional questions, multi-step flow, and explicit receipt pages.
Browser runtime. Launch owned browser contexts with resource limits, isolation, domain policies, trace redaction, cancellation, safe session storage, and a visible local mode for owner observation.
SDK. Implement the chapter 10 interfaces including form snapshots, field plans, read-back validation, and receipt observations.
Fill primitives. Support text, email, phone, textarea, select, radio, checkbox, date, file upload, autocomplete, and character-limited answers, reporting unsupported controls explicitly.
Challenge fixtures. Model CAPTCHA and MFA states with synthetic challenge screens without implementing bypass, persisting exceptions while other jobs continue.

gates.requirement: Filled values read back exactly, including underlying option values where relevant.
Upload validation distinguishes selected, uploading, accepted, and failed states.
Conditional fields are reinspected and required answers cannot be missed.
A changed question invalidates an old answer plan.
Challenge detection creates a resumable exception without stopping other queue items.
A generic banner or HTTP 200 cannot create confirmed-submission state.
The dry-run mode cannot accidentally invoke a final external commit, including implicit submission through Enter or a field-change event.

phases.title: Actual submission vertical slice

tickets.text: Policy gate. Implement the complete precommit checklist and immutable intent binding, verifying profile, policy, destination, form, answer, document, duplicate, and budget constraints.
Commit engine. Persist intent and in-flight attempt before the final action, enforcing exclusive commit ownership, cancellation checks, and exact adapter routing.
Receipt verification. Implement strong success, definitive validation failure, and unknown-outcome classification, storing evidence with job and application correlation.
Reconciliation. Recover from an in-flight record without replaying the final click, reading the mock ATS account and receipt record to resolve accepted versus unknown states.

First real adapter. Choose one high-yield portal family from current candidate opportunities, implement and test its actual final submission and receipt behavior, then run a genuine controlled application under the recorded policy.

gates.requirement: Auto-submit mode completes the mock workflow without a per-application owner click.
Each confirmed state has independently correlated receipt evidence.
Every crash case avoids blind duplicate submission; ambiguous cases remain explicit.
Revocation immediately before commit prevents the final action.
A stale worker cannot acquire a new valid commit capability.
At least one genuine, appropriate live submission is receipt-verified before the adapter is labeled live-verified.
If a live prerequisite is unavailable, code completion and live verification are reported separately, and unrelated engineering continues.

tickets.text: Coverage analysis. Group eligible jobs by portal family, employer-specific variant, account requirement, and current failure reason, prioritizing adapters by expected additional suitable submissions per engineering effort.

Adapter increments. Add the next high-yield families, normally from Recruitee, Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby browser forms, each with detection, field mapping, validation, commit, and receipt implementation.
Variant fixtures. Capture sanitized real form structures and rebuild representative variants in the mock environment, including employer-added questions and localized labels.
Drift detection. Monitor structural fingerprints and missing expected controls, pausing only the affected adapter version when its contract breaks.
Support matrix. Publish discovery, inspection, fill, account, commit, receipt, and reconciliation coverage separately with last-tested dates and known limitations.

gates.requirement: Every added adapter passes the common SDK contract and portal-specific fixtures.
Each supported variant has at least one successful synthetic receipt and relevant negative cases.
A new unknown mandatory field stops that application before commitment.
A drifted adapter cannot degrade into unrestricted generic clicking.
Each live-verified label has a genuine private receipt and date; untested variants remain explicitly provisional.
At least two portal families complete the full synthetic pipeline without special workflow code outside the adapter boundary.

phases.title: Accounts, secure handoffs, and exception resolution

tickets.text: Account registry. Map candidate identity to employer domain and applicant account, storing only vault references with creation status, session validity, and last verification time.

Signup workflow. Fill supported ordinary signup forms using approved identity, generate unique credentials, and store them securely before a workflow can depend on them, detecting verification, MFA, payment, and unusual agreement steps.
Challenge handoff. Preserve progress, create a scoped session handle, expose a visible local resume route, and expire stale handles, without implementing CAPTCHA bypass.
tickets.nextAction: Preserve solved session state and prove adapter-specific live challenge continuation. See docs/evidence/WORKFLOW-RECOVERY.md.

tickets.text: Exception inbox. Show the exact question or blocker, affected job, suggested supported answer if any, evidence, and actions to resolve, defer, skip, or open a session.
Propagation and resumption. An approved answer resolves semantically equivalent pending questions within its scope, and the entire affected form is revalidated before commitment.
tickets.nextAction: Resume all affected applications and validate exact answer meanings across every supported adapter.

gates.requirement: Supported signup stores credentials safely and never exposes them to model prompts or logs.
A lost signup response does not automatically create a second account.
CAPTCHA/MFA generates a usable handoff while unrelated queue work continues.
Handoff URLs/handles expire, are owner-bound, and cannot control another session.
User interaction and automation cannot race the final submit.
Resolving one answer does not incorrectly propagate to differently worded legal or sponsorship questions.
A resumed expired form is rebuilt safely, while an ambiguous prior commit is reconciled first.

remoteVerification.covers: Account vault and one-action signup checkpoint only. The handoff-lease and visible-handoff checkpoints have no recorded cross-platform run.

phases.nextAction: Complete solved-session continuation, all-adapter exact answer gates and affected-application resumption; verify with synthetic CI before reclosing P10.

tickets.text: OAuth lifecycle. Implement least-sufficient scopes, secure token storage, refresh, disconnect, revocation handling, and actionable reconnect states, documenting testing-mode versus deployed-app limitations.
Narrow message acquisition. Query only relevant time windows and application and account contexts, fetch minimal fields, and avoid retaining unrelated email.

Correlation. Match messages to pending applications using expected recipient, employer or sender domain, role or requisition ID, application ID, and timing, preserving uncertainty where several jobs could match.
Verification links. Follow only links bound to a pending signup and a validated destination chain, rejecting unexpected redirects or instructions to disclose secrets.
Outcome updates. Classify receipt, interview, rejection, or ambiguous message with supporting evidence, without automatically replying to recruiters or accepting interview times.

gates.requirement: OAuth refresh and revocation produce correct state transitions without exposing tokens.
Synthetic unrelated messages never trigger actions or appear in application records.
Account-created and application-received messages are correctly distinguished.
Two roles at the same employer do not receive the same receipt unless identity evidence supports it.
Unexpected verification-link domains are rejected.
Duplicate email delivery creates one outcome event.
The app remains useful with Gmail disconnected.

phases.title: Bounded multi-agent orchestration and cost optimization

tickets.text: Graph contracts. Implement extractor, match analyst, drafter, form-answer planner, critic, and bounded repair nodes with typed input and output and capability restrictions.
Checkpointing. Save calculation checkpoints with graph, prompt, and schema versions, resuming compatible work and explicitly migrating or restarting incompatible pure preparation.
Batching. Batch only independent similarly sized tasks, require item IDs, validate each result separately, and split on truncation or context pressure.
Dynamic routing. Select eligible free models by measured task quality, context needs, health, and latency, keeping model pinning subject to the free-only firewall.

Evaluation and ablation. Compare the deterministic and template baseline, single-model generation, and drafter-plus-critic on the same held-out jobs, measuring claim errors, correction rate, latency, and requests per accepted packet.

gates.requirement: Agent execution has bounded steps, time, tokens, and request count.
Graph replay cannot perform or repeat a final submission.
Batch contamination, duplicate IDs, missing items, and truncated output are detected.
Free-only routing remains enforced under fallback and manual model selection.
The measured multi-agent variant improves a declared metric or is not enabled by default.
A 50-request simulation exhausts predictably, preserves reserve accounting, and defers work without falsifying success.

tickets.text: Background runtime. Package a launcher and an owner-approved startup mechanism with graceful shutdown, crash restart, health checks, and configuration migration.
Scheduling. Implement source-specific polling, queue priorities, daily targets, browser concurrency limits, quiet hours for notifications, and Europe/Amsterdam day boundaries.
Operations dashboard. Show actual stage counts, confirmed evidence, unresolved ambiguity, the needs-help queue, next work, the model quota estimate, and stop controls.
Capacity testing. Run synthetic day workloads with varied fit, model latency, account friction, portal errors, and challenges, measuring bottlenecks and memory growth.
Controlled live ramp. Under active policy, progress from the verified canary to small batches and then toward the requested target, stopping or isolating affected routes on correctness regressions.

gates.requirement: Closing Codex does not stop the application runtime.
Restarting Windows or the worker resumes non-ambiguous work and reconciles in-flight attempts.
Sleep/wake and network-loss tests do not cause duplicate commits.
A 24-hour synthetic soak shows no unbounded queue, memory, disk, or retry growth.
Pause and emergency stop behave as documented, including the limitation for already-sent requests.
The dashboard can explain the target shortfall using measured counts.
Live ramp evidence is genuine; reaching 50 is not a release claim unless actually observed.

phases.title: Fully deployable server and hybrid profiles

tickets.text: Server images and Compose. Build reproducible images with pinned browser and runtime compatibility, PostgreSQL, persistent artifacts, an authenticated API, TLS configuration, health checks, and restart policies.
Secrets and storage. Support environment-mounted or external secret-store references without baking credentials into images, with S3-compatible storage contract tests and encryption configuration.
Hybrid transport. Implement outbound worker registration, authenticated command delivery, owner binding, command expiry, replay protection, lease renewal, and receipt acknowledgment.
Secure browser handoff. Provide owner-authenticated, expiring access to a single waiting server browser session over a reviewed private transport, never exposing raw debug endpoints publicly.
Migration. Export and import candidate and application state consistently, drain active commits, reconcile uncertainty, move artifact manifests, and require session reauthentication when necessary.

gates.requirement: A clean server deployment completes the full mock application workflow with the owner's PC disconnected.
Hybrid mode completes the same workflow with a local browser worker and server-owned state.
Replayed, expired, wrong-owner, and wrong-intent commands are rejected.
Loss of server connectivity prevents new local commits after lease/authorization expiry.
Database and browser-control ports are not publicly exposed in the production profile.
Local-to-server migration preserves application identity, packets, policy versions, and receipts.
TLS/authentication, backup, and resource requirements are documented and tested.

phases.title: Security, fault injection, restore, and release gates

tickets.text: Threat review. Test malicious job descriptions, email instructions, document payloads, unsafe imported URLs, untrusted model output, and attempts to widen execution authority.
Crash matrix. Execute every commit boundary under process kill, network loss, worker duplication, lease expiry, queue redelivery, and receipt-write failure.
Recovery drills. Back up, restore, rekey where supported, rotate credentials, revoke authorization, and simulate restoring a database older than external applications.
tickets.nextAction: Complete whole-installation restore, signup/mailbox fencing and artifact consistency drills.

tickets.text: Supply-chain checks. Audit dependencies, pin CI actions where practical, generate an SBOM, scan release artifacts for secrets, and document the provenance of copied code.
tickets.nextAction: Generate and validate release SBOM and artifact scans; retain dependency audit checks.

tickets.text: Soak and performance. Run 72-hour synthetic operation with outages and quota resets, measuring resource bounds, reconciliation lag, queue fairness, and parser drift response.

gates.requirement: No critical unresolved finding can permit unauthorized submission, secret disclosure, wrong-owner access, or blind duplicate replay.
Zero duplicate external records occur in the supported mock crash suite; unresolved outcomes are retained honestly.
All free-only adversarial pricing/fallback tests pass.
A restored system remains commit-disabled until the external-submission gap is reconciled.
Backup restoration verifies database consistency and artifact checksums.
The 72-hour synthetic soak completes with bounded resource usage and no silently lost tasks.
Real adapter claims are limited to the tested variants and dates.

Cohort reporting. Compare sources, role families, seniority, sponsorship signals, and document variants using fixed application cohorts and suitable observation windows.

Score calibration. Evaluate whether high fit scores correspond to better reviewed relevance and eventually better outcomes, publishing no interview probabilities before enough reliable labeled outcomes exist.
Quality regression loop. Turn corrected facts, rejected claims, misclassified forms, and adapter drift into sanitized regression fixtures.
Controlled experiments. Compare approved wording or ordering variants without applying twice to the same job or weakening truthfulness, recording experiment assignments before outcomes are known.
